Ross Gerber Calls Cybertruck Another Tesla Failure
Gerber, co-founder, president, and CEO of
Gerber Kawasaki Wealth & Investment Management
, took to
X
to criticize Tesla following Musk’s announcement.
“Another failure for Tesla and Elon,” Gerber wrote, arguing that the company is struggling as an electric vehicle manufacturer and questioning whether its autonomous-driving ambitions can succeed.
He also took aim at Tesla’s Full Self-Driving technology, saying it is “not even close to safe enough yet for Cybercab to scale.”
Gerber also questioned the potential profitability of Tesla’s robotaxi business, concluding bluntly: “Tesla is cooked.”

Another failure for tesla and Elon. Not surprising to end the cybertruck. Basically tesla is not an EV company and sells only one model. Yet FSD is not even close to safe enough yet for cybercab to scale and that businesses economics are not so good… tesla is cooked.
Gary Black Flags Tesla’s Missed Pickup Opportunity
Investor
Gary Black
also criticized Tesla for missing an opportunity to develop a more conventional-looking electric pickup modeled after the refreshed Model Y.

He argued that such a vehicle could have helped Tesla tap into the global pickup market, which sells an estimated 6 million to 7 million units annually, without significantly cannibalizing its existing lineup.
“Such a missed opportunity,” Black wrote on X, arguing that Tesla’s failure to pursue the strategy reflects a broader lack of strategic marketing expertise.
He also referenced his June 2025 analysis, which estimated that Cybertruck deliveries for fiscal 2025 were on track to reach just around 20,000 units.

Musk Shifts Focus From Cybertruck to Cybercab
Musk said that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck production at its Gigafactory Texas facility around mid-2027 to free up capacity for increased Cybercab manufacturing.

In a separate post, Musk shared an image of the astronaut dummy placed inside his personal Tesla Roadster, which was launched into space aboard SpaceX’s Falcon Heavy rocket during its 2018 test flight.
Cybertruck Sales Fall Short of Musk’s Ambitions
Unveiled in 2019, the Cybertruck was initially expected to enter production in 2021 but faced multiple delays before deliveries began in November 2023.

Musk had targeted annual production of 250,000 units. However, estimates suggest Tesla sold just 7,000 to 8,000 Cybertrucks in the third quarter of 2026, translating to an annualized pace of roughly 28,000 to 32,000 units.
